messages:
ops-oncall: noticing elevated pod evictions and slow queue drain in apac-syd since ~08:00 UTC. Dedicated slices showing traffic pileup, latency spikes for heavy-context requests. escalating to infra.
infra-eng: thanks — any obvious node OOM or GPU hardware alerts?
ops-oncall: no hardware alarms. kube evictions citing imagepuller/oom? pattern looks like bursty create/delete, survivor pods end up stuck Pending for minutes.
runtime-eng: can you paste recent events from one affected node?
ops-oncall: sure
ops-oncall: ```
# kubectl -n inference describe node gpu-node-az1
Events:
  09:02:12 Warning Eviction kubelet eviction manager: eviction threshold met
  09:02:14 Normal Preempted pod "batch-probe-xx"
  09:03:00 Warning Failed scheduling: 0/12 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient memory, 2 Insufficient gpu, 7 NodeAffinity.
```
platform-sre: looks like scheduling pressure + noisy batch jobs creating ephemeral pods that saturate the kubelet's reclaim loop. That can cause kube-proxy churn and delay pod admission.
infra-eng: check our warm pool / reserve accounting — maybe IDs weren't released after preemptions. patchy reserve leaks have come up before.
product-ops: customer impact? any SLA alerts?
ops-oncall: few P50 latency alerts on Dedicated routes, no customer-facing 5xx spike yet. Biz impact limited but risk of degrade if pile persists.
sre-runbooks-bot: runbook suggestion: follow "queue-backfill-and-provisioning" checklist and consider temporary soft-shift to other regions. (link: https://internal/runbooks/queue-backfill)
infra-eng: starting triage: 1) identify high-churn namespaces 2) drain/cordon worst nodes 3) throttle batch job admission 4) verify reserve pool counts
nora: I'll grep scheduler logs for bind failures and post binding latencies.
runtime-eng: parallel: enable a short cooldown on GPU idle reclamation to stop rapid create/destroy thrash. toggles are in cfg-store: `inference.cluster.reclaim.cooldown_s`.
ops-oncall: set cooldown to 180s on apac-syd? currently 30s
infra-eng: do it, but also ensure we don't overcommit. making change now.
infra-eng: `kubectl -n infra set configmap reclaim-config --from-literal=cooldown_s=180` -> applied
platform-sre: migrating some Dedicated routes off apac-syd gradually. initiating soft-shift (weighted 70/30 to eu-west while we stabilize).
release-coordinator: FYI this will increment cross-region egress costs — tracking in JIRA INF-4123.
product-ops: thanks — keep me posted, will notify a handful of customers on Dedicated if latency persists.
ops-oncall: cordoning two noisy nodes now to stop scheduling new pods.
ops-oncall: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-az1 && kubectl cordon gpu-node-az3`
infra-eng: eviction queue cleared on those nodes, but backlog still in the route queue. looks like router didn't drop queued requests on failover. adding short ttl for route queue entries.
runtime-eng: added `router.queue.ttl_s=30` in config; now router will fail fast to trigger client fallbacks instead of long queuing.
ops-oncall: immediate P95 latency dropped ~25% after queue-ttl change and soft-shift. still seeing intermittent Pending pods for heavy-context containers.
infra-eng: found a reservation accounting bug: when preemptible probe pods were killed by kubelet, reservation tokens weren't returned to the warm pool. opening a hotfix PR.
infra-eng: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/merge/PR-1498
infra-eng: patch will reconcile reserve counters on pod delete events and add metrics.
nora: scheduler bind latency spike correlated with ipam delays when many pods init network simultaneously. adding jitter to startup of batch jobs (control-plane change) helps.
platform-sre: next steps for runbook: 1) add explicit step to check reserve-token leak, 2) include guidance to bump reclaim cooldown, 3) recommend router queue-ttl change for high-churn incidents, 4) add checklist for soft-shift cost approval path.
ops-oncall: can someone open a runbook PR? I'll draft the text.
product-ops: also add owner for customer comms and a template message.
ops-oncall: creating runbook PR now: https://git.internal/docs/runbooks/merge/RB-221
ops-oncall: action items assigned: INF-4123 (cost tracking), INF-4124 (hotfix deploy), INF-4125 (runbook PR), INF-4126 (batch job jitter rollout)
release-coordinator: scheduling hotfix deploy to apac-syd canary at 10:15 UTC, full roll at 10:30 if green.
infra-eng: hotfix canary passed, promotes to regional rollout.
ops-oncall: monitoring — pod Pending count steadily decreasing, P95 latency back to baseline. leaving nodes cordoned 30m for stability.
platform-sre: runbook note: for multi-tenant Dedicated slices, prefer soft-shift + queue-ttl change before full-slice failover to avoid large rebalancing spikes.
product-ops: excellent. can we add cost guardrail that auto-alerts when cross-region egress spends spike > $X/hr during incidents?
infra-eng: added a ticket INF-4127 for cost guardrail alerting.
ops-oncall: closing incident thread — will follow up with post-incident summary and link to runbook PR after merge.
sre-runbooks-bot: postmortem reminder: please fill the incident timeline and impact in the postmortem template within 48h. (https://internal/postmortems)
infra-eng: quick note for the postmortem: cause = reservation-token leak + aggressive reclaim cooldown + IPAM startup contention; mitigations = hotfix, increased reclaim cooldown, router queue ttl, batch startup jitter, runbook edits.
ops-oncall: thanks all :thumbsup:
platform-sre: assigning a 2-week follow-up to validate reserve counters on long-running spikes.
nora: will attach scheduler logs and metrics to the postmortem.
ops-oncall: last status: stable. closing thread."
